title: SDK invoker: heterogeneous-schema validation, progressive retries & stream-resume helpers
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Current SDK helpers validate and invoke function/tool schemas using a single canonical shape which fails when model-produced payloads vary slightly by language/serializer or when clients adapt schema versions at runtime. This results in brittle function calling, surprising rejections, and poor developer ergonomics during streaming or partial responses.

Goal: Provide a cross-language invoker library that performs tolerant schema validation (structural/field-level coercions and soft warnings), enforces safe invocation (idempotency keys, dedupe tokens), and supports progressive retry/backoff with stream-resume tokens so long-running or partial streamed outputs can be resumed without duplicating side-effects. Integrate tracing and token-level telemetry to make retries and resumptions observable in Console.

Scope: Design and implement APIs for Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs including: schema adapters (multiple allowed shapes), runtime coercion rules (string->enum, number coercion, missing optional fields), invocation wrapper that: attaches idempotency metadata, performs preflight validation with configurable strictness, orchestrates progressive retry/backoff for transient errors (with jitter and per-chunk epoch), and enables generation/consumption of resume tokens for streaming flows. Provide developer examples, unit/integration tests, and migration guidance for existing function-calling integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-language API design doc approved by SDK leads explaining validator modes: strict, tolerant, and compatibility (linked in links)
Python/TS/Go SDKs ship invoker helper that exposes: validate(schema, payload, mode), invoke_with_guard(schema, payload, options) and stream_resume(token)
Invoker attaches an idempotency token to calls and exposes a stable resume token for streamed responses
Progressive retry strategy implemented with configurable max_attempts, backoff_strategy and per-chunk checkpoints
End-to-end integration tests demonstrating resume from mid-stream without duplicated side-effects against local runtime mock
Telemetry spans emitted for validation failures, retry attempts, and resume events and visible in Console trace view
Migration guide and code examples for popular patterns (webhook side-effects, database write idempotency) published in docs repo
